rules.title: Lessors barred from charging application or other fees beyond first, last, security deposit and lock change
rules.requirement: Before a tenancy begins, a landlord (lessor) may require payment only of first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit, and a lock fee. Application, screening, pet, cleaning, amenity and similar fees are forbidden for landlords.
rules.coverage_text: Lessors of residential rental units in Massachusetts; no exemptions are stated in the text.
rules.key_value: Only first, last, security deposit, and locks may be charged before tenancy
rules.penalty: Described as treble damages and attorney's fees in a cited federal case (Perry v. Equity Residential Management, LLC).
rules.ambiguity_note: Text says the law has been in effect since the 1970s but gives no specific date. Source is a secondary landlord-association page describing state law.
rules.quoted_span: It states that prior to the beginning of a tenancy, no lessor may require payment for anything except first, last, security, and locks (MGL Ch 186 Section 15B).

rules.title: Licensed brokers may charge fees to prospective tenants subject to written disclosure
rules.requirement: Licensed brokers may charge fees (including application or screening fees) to prospective tenants. The broker must give the applicant written notice of the fee amount, time and manner of payment, and whether it is contingent on a lease being signed, at the first personal meeting.
rules.coverage_text: Licensed brokers or salespersons finding dwelling accommodations for prospective tenants for a fee; a landlord acting as own broker is uncertain.
rules.key_value: Written notice of broker fee signed by applicant at first personal meeting
rules.ambiguity_note: Whether a landlord who is also a licensed broker may charge such a fee is unresolved in the text. Secondary source summarizing regulations.
rules.quoted_span: In addition to holding a valid license, the broker has to tell the applicant in writing the amount of the broker’s fee, the time and manner of payment, and whether it is contingent on the owner and applicant actually entering into a lease or rental agreement.
